title: Three Practical Raw-Fish Techniques from ATK: Tuna Bowl with Blanching, Ceviche (Leche de Tigre), and Gravlax

locations.name: United States
locations.basis: Transcript mentions US context for fish sourcing (01:01–01:05).

summary: America’s Test Kitchen’s Techniquely episode demonstrates three accessible raw-fish preparations anchored in careful sourcing and hands-on technique: a tuna bowl that uses hot-water blanching to firm the exterior and a flavorful marinade; a ceviche-style preparation with leche de tigre and a lime-based emulsion that gently “cooks” the fish through acid; and a gravlax-style salmon cure that relies on salt, sugar, and dill over several days. The video emphasizes starting with properly handled fish (often frozen and defrosted under controlled conditions), precise knife work for clean cuts, marination timing to balance flavor and texture, and practical plating and garnishing ideas. Safety notes cover parasite considerations, the relative risks of raw fish for certain populations, and the distinction between acid- versus heat-induced changes in fish proteins.
topics: Tuna marinade components (rice wine vinegar, soy, ginger, sugar)
Knife technique: heel of blade and pulling motion
Marination time and texture control in ceviche
Gravlax curing with salt, brown sugar, and dill
Garnishes for raw-fish dishes (corn nuts, popcorn, creme fraiche)

sections.title: Tuna prep and blanching for a marinated raw-fish bowl
sections.description: Introduces tuna-based preparation and the concept of using heat (blanching) to firm the fish exterior and improve flavor absorption. Marinade components shown include seasoned rice wine vinegar, soy sauce, fresh ginger, and sugar; beginning notes on fish freshness and sourcing are discussed.

sections.title: Assembling the tuna bowl and finishing textures
sections.description: Demonstrates assembling the bowl: layering seasoned sushi rice, blanched spinach, and assorted garnishes, then slicing tuna into neat blocks and finishing with a dressing and sesame for texture contrast.

sections.title: Ceviche prep: leche de tigre and lime-based marinade
sections.description: Details the Peruvian-style leche de tigre and its use as a lime-acid emulsion to marinate fish. Explains how acid denatures proteins to firm fish, emphasizes that acid does not sterilize, and covers flavor components (garlic, aji amarillo, olive oil, salt).

sections.title: Gravlax: salt cure for salmon and slicing technique
sections.description: Outlines the gravlax process: coating a salmon filet with a salt–sugar rub, curing for about three days in the fridge with weights, rinsing and drying, then slicing on a 45-degree angle to yield wide, translucent pieces with dense texture.

sections.title: Closing tasting and recap
sections.description: Concludes with a tasting of the three techniques and recap of key safety notes, marination control, and plating ideas, encouraging viewer experimentation and comments.
